meta.title: Protected preparation and secretless pull-request validation
meta.author: Codex manager

feature.problem_statement: Infra and runner-config pull-request-controlled validation currently receives Nexus or private-repository credentials, allowing candidate code to exfiltrate persistent credentials.
goals: Move all authenticated preparation into workflows and scripts loaded from protected main.
Give candidate validation only digest-bound non-secret artifacts.
Keep activation and bootstrap reconciliation fail closed.
non_goals: Dispatching activation or mutating live infrastructure.
Making the current infra pull request directly deployable.
scope_in: Focused protected-main prerequisite workflows in infra and runner-config.
Secretless updates to infra PR 1070 and runner-config PR 27.
Authenticated protected-main runner-config revision verification and post-merge lock candidate production.
scope_out: Main PR merges and live activation.

requirements.statement: Pull-request-controlled workflows, scripts, lockfiles, and jobs MUST receive no Nexus credentials, deploy key, SSH agent, or persistent credential.
requirements.rationale: Candidate code must not be able to exfiltrate trusted credentials.

requirements.statement: A protected-main workflow MUST prepare only fixed allowlisted exact-hash Nexus artifacts and, for infra, one fixed runner-config SHA, without executing candidate code.

Untrusted validation MUST run in a separate secretless job and verify a manifest binding candidate SHA, trusted workflow SHA, runner SHA where applicable, and every artifact digest before executing candidate tests.
requirements.rationale: Safe artifacts must not be substitutable or stale.

requirements.statement: The protected activation producer MUST authenticate to the GitHub API and prove runner-config main is protected and resolves to the exact approved SHA without unauthenticated ls-remote.
requirements.rationale: Private repository revision trust requires authenticated protected-branch evidence.

requirements.statement: Bootstrap and validation tool acquisition MUST use fixed Nexus paths and hashes only, with no public fallback, while the checked-in infra PR bootstrap stays unsyncable.
requirements.rationale: Tool provenance and deployment safety must remain fail closed.

requirements.statement: A protected-main post-merge workflow MUST generate a digest-bound lock-materialization candidate artifact for separate review and MUST NOT apply or commit it automatically.
requirements.rationale: The future merge SHA cannot be safely embedded in the current PR.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given a candidate modifies any PR workflow or script, when PR validation runs, then no candidate-controlled job receives a secret expression, deploy key, SSH agent, or persisted checkout credential.

Given a trusted preparation event, when artifacts are fetched, then the executed workflow and preparer come from protected main and candidate-controlled URLs, commands, scripts, and lockfiles are never used.
Given a missing, altered, stale, or cross-PR preparation bundle, when candidate validation starts, then manifest verification fails before candidate tests execute.
Given runner-config main is missing, unprotected, or resolves to a different SHA, when activation production starts, then it fails before cluster or signing work.
Given validation or bootstrap needs Python, Helm, or kubectl, when acquisition occurs, then only fixed Nexus URLs with exact hashes are accepted and the PR bootstrap Application remains excluded.
Given infra is merged to protected main, when the lock-materialization workflow runs, then it emits a reviewable exact-revision patch artifact but performs no commit, sync, or apply.

test_plan.approach: Parse workflows and scripts; reject secret expressions, SSH/deploy-key use, credential environment, or persisted checkouts in all candidate jobs.
Assert pull_request_target/base-source trust, exact workflow/preparer SHA verification, fixed allowlists, and absence of candidate execution in trusted jobs.
Exercise manifest verification negatives for candidate SHA, trusted SHA, runner SHA, artifact digest, missing file, and additional file drift.
Mock authenticated GitHub branch API responses for exact protected success and missing, unprotected, or mismatched failure.
Scan changed workflows and acquisition code for public endpoints, mutable URLs, missing hashes, and active bootstrap Application resources.
Validate post-merge-only trigger, protected-main API binding, patch artifact digest, and absence of commit/apply/sync commands.

review_checks: Review every candidate job and workflow for credential reachability.
validation_checks: Static secret-boundary suite passes in both repositories.

review_checks: Review event source, workflow SHA verification, allowlists, and job isolation.
Review manifest canonicalization and all SHA/digest bindings.
validation_checks: All bundle negative fixtures fail before test execution.

review_checks: Review authenticated API request and protected-branch checks.
Review all Python, Helm, and kubectl acquisition paths and bootstrap kustomization.
Review post-merge artifact-only behavior and exact revision binding.

perspectives.summary: Secrets exist only in protected-main preparation jobs; candidate execution occurs only after job isolation with verified non-secret bundles.
Base-controlled pull_request_target prerequisites are required before candidate workflows are made secretless.
All inputs are fixed allowlisted Nexus objects or an exact authenticated protected runner SHA and are digest-bound.
The current bootstrap remains unsyncable and post-merge output is a review artifact, never an automatic apply.

council.consensus_summary: Proceed through focused prerequisite PRs first, then remove credentials from both existing main PRs and validate the complete boundary.
